title: Pin semantic affordances for tag / semver / commit-hash in SDK
creator: Lena Chen
description:
Problem statement: Customers expect predictable and auditable behavior when they pin models in the Redwood API/SDK using tags (e.g., 'stable'), semver ranges (e.g., ^1.2.0), or raw commit hashes. Our current surface is under-specified in edge cases: mixed-pin requests (tag + hash), tag-to-hash TTLs, semver range precedence vs explicit hashes, and how runtime fallbacks choose compatible quantized/variant builds. This ticket defines the semantic contract we will publish and implement across SDK and runtime so that developers can reason about rollouts, canaries, and emergency rollbacks without surprising model resolution.

Goals:
- Define deterministic resolution order for pins: explicit-hash > exact-semver > semver-range > tag > latest-fallback.
- Specify time-bound semantics for tag pins: tags resolve to a stable hash and expose a server-side "resolved_at" TTL and audit-id to make cached decisions reproducible for a short window.
- Allow opaque "pinned_by_policy" metadata on resolved responses to aid observability (not required for clients to parse).
- Ensure SDK surface exposes clear constructors for pin types and a resolution diagnostics API for debugging resolved hashes and fallback reasons.
- Keep backwards compatibility with existing simple pin-by-string behavior while adding opt-in strict modes (e.g., require_hash=true) for enterprises.

API surface (examples):
- SDK pin object examples (pseudo):
  - pin: "commit:cafef00d..."  // explicit hash
  - pin: "semver:1.4.2"        // exact semver
  - pin: "semver:^1.3.0"       // semver range
  - pin: "tag:stable"         // tag alias

- New SDK helper (pseudo-TS):
  const pin = Pin.byTag('stable')
  const pin = Pin.bySemver('^1.3.0')
  const pin = Pin.byHash('cafef00d')

- Call-level option: {strictPin: true|false}
  - strictPin=true: runtime will reject any resolution that does not match the requested pin semantics (e.g., semver mismatch) instead of falling back.

Resolution algorithm (summary):
1. If request contains an explicit commit hash, resolve to that exact build if available. If missing, return 404-model-not-found unless allow_fallback is set.
2. If exact semver is provided, match exact release tag -> hash.
3. If semver range, choose highest compatible release that satisfies range and is active in the model catalog.
4. If tag provided, consult tag->hash mapping with attached "tag_ttl_seconds". If the client provides a cached resolved_hash and cache_age < tag_ttl, honor client cache; otherwise resolve fresh and return resolved_hash + resolved_at in response metadata.
5. After initial resolution, runtime evaluates variant compatibility (quantization, hardware). If resolved build is incompatible with current node, attempt same-hash compatible variant; otherwise, apply configured fallback policy: model-variant > downgraded-sequence > region-fallback > capacity-fallback.

Observability and auditability:
- Responses will include headers/metadata: X-Model-Resolved-Hash, X-Model-Resolved-At, X-Model-Pin-Type, X-Model-Pin-Input.
- SDK will surface a resolutionDiagnostic() call that returns a short timeline of resolution steps for last request (string-encoded, meant for logs). Example: "requested=tag:stable -> tag->hash=abc123 @2025-03-07T12:21Z -> variant=quantized-int8 -> node=us-west-2-a -> used-fallback=none".
- Console feature: display pin resolution history per-call for customers on Dedicated/Private fleets (privacy-safe, uses internal audit ids).

Backwards compatibility & migration:
- Existing string pin behavior continues to work: library will heuristically detect format (prefix commit:, semver:, tag:). We will add a deprecation-warning in SDK when ambiguous pin strings are used (e.g., '1.2.3' could be semver or tag). Encourage explicit Pin.bySemver/Pin.byTag constructors.
- Provide a one-command migration script in SDK (redwood models migrate-pins) that audits usage, suggests strictPin adoption, and generates a sample mapping file for tags.

Security considerations:
- Prevent tag squatting and untrusted tag writes: tag-to-hash resolution requires catalog write ACLs already guarded by model onboarding flows. Call out that tag updates must require a signed release workflow (covered by onboarding policy).

notes: Open questions: should semver-range resolution consider pre-release tags by default? (proposal: ignore pre-release unless explicitly requested via 'include_prerelease=true')
Risk: if tag TTL is too long, customers doing rapid rollouts may see stale models. Operational recommendation: expose tag_ttl per-tag and allow per-call override for critical requests.
Monitoring: add alert when resolved_hash churn rate for a given tag exceeds threshold (possible misconfigured CI pushing tags).
